subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed native `sessions_spawn` keep the accepted asynchronous response and later terminalize with a typed/logged startup failure, or should it preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: That choice changes gateway wait semantics, subagent registry/session state, user-visible diagnostics, and compatibility for the documented non-blocking spawn contract, so automation should not pick the permanent API behavior alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the documented accepted response and add visible typed/logged terminal startup failure state in session history, subagent list, gateway wait, and completion handling.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation before the accepted response so `sessions_spawn` fails fast, accepting extra spawn latency and compatibility review.

options.title: Resolve Through Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open while replacing the conflicting lifecycle PR with a current-main implementation that proves the sandbox-specific Docker path.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the documented accepted response and add visible typed/logged terminal startup failure state in session history, subagent list, gateway wait, and completion handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The product/API choice crosses the subagent lifecycle and terminal-outcome surfaces where steipete has the clearest historical ownership signal.
